title: Standard basis operator method for ground-state and temperature properties of single and two-component Bose-Hubbard model
abstract: We formulate an improved standard basis operator (SBO) method for the single and two-component Bose-Hubbard model in three dimensions. In the first case, nonzero temperature predictions are qualitatively and quantitatively enhanced by taking into account necessary number of on-site states, not just three as in previous works. Performance of the final numerical calculations is also improved by asymptotic analysis of the self-consistent equations near the critical line. Obtained results are compared with Monte-Carlo, tensor networks, Quantum Rotor Approach and experimental data. In the two-component case, SBO generalizes rather poorly, being able to account for intra-species thermal and quantum fluctuations, but not the inter-species ones. Deeper reasons for this situation are discussed. Still however, non-trivial deformation of the phase diagrams is predicted, together with first-order phase transitions steered by the changes in chemical potential.
summary: The paper introduces an enhanced Standard Basis Operator method to calculate the properties of the Bose-Hubbard model. It improves upon prior work by correctly accounting for more on-site states at finite temperatures and predicts complex phase transitions in multi-component systems. The methodology is highly relevant for understanding strongly correlated quantum gases.
main_problem: The authors aim to develop an improved theoretical method for calculating both ground-state and finite-temperature properties of the Bose-Hubbard model.
main_result: They successfully enhanced predictions by accounting for a necessary number of on-site states, while also predicting non-trivial phase diagram deformations in the two-component case.
method: The core method is an improved Standard Basis Operator (SBO) approach formulated within a nonperturbative Green's function framework, utilizing Random Phase Approximation (RPA).
model_or_system: The study focuses on the single and two-component Bose-Hubbard model in three dimensions, governed by a Hamiltonian involving hopping ($J$), on-site interaction ($U$), and chemical potential ($\mu$).
key_observables: Phase boundary, excitation spectra, boson occupancies (D_alpha), critical temperature (T_c/J).
important_parameters: Interaction strength to hopping ratio (U/J), chemical potential ($\mu/U$), and temperature ($T/J$).
main_assumptions: The method relies on the RPA for decoupling higher-order Green's functions, which is noted to violate algebraic rules in multi-component systems.
figures_summary: Figures compare critical lines (SBO vs. QRA vs. TNS), show lobe structures at different temperatures, and illustrate how increasing the number of retained local Fock states improves accuracy.
paper_structure: The paper develops the SBO method using Green's functions, applies RPA to solve for these functions in momentum space, derives self-consistency equations from spectral theorems, and discusses limitations regarding multi-component extensions and numerical stability near phase transitions.
why_interesting: This work provides advanced theoretical tools (improved SBO) to study interacting quantum gases, offering quantitative improvements over previous approximations by systematically handling local Hilbert space truncation effects.
